# ADB device inspection and acquisition

REA inspects connected Android devices, reads device state, and transfers
files and packages through the caller's `adb` binary. Emulators, USB
devices, and network devices participate alike: REA neither starts nor
manages them and never installs platform tools. Every operation composes a
fixed adb argument vector — caller values occupy positional arguments only
and are quoted when adb forwards them to the device shell.

The adb client may start its local server on first device query; that is adb
client behavior, recorded in the tool result when observed.
`inspect_adb_client` probes only the binary and never contacts the server.

## Supply tools

Use any Android platform-tools `adb` (verified with 34.0.5). Select it
through the environment:

```sh
# Optional: absolute path to the adb binary; without it, adb resolves from PATH.
export REA_ADB_PATH=/absolute/path/to/adb
```

REA never installs the Android SDK, an emulator, or a system image.
Readiness is `rea inspect-adb-client`: it runs `adb version` and reports the
resolved binary, its version, and where it was selected from. A missing
binary reports `capability_unavailable` with the `REA_ADB_PATH` remediation
rather than attempting an installation.
The `binary_session` inventory uses the same bounded client-version probe; it
does not query devices, start the adb server, or establish that a requested
serial is reachable. Device state is checked by each device operation.

## Answer an analyst question

```sh
# Device identity
rea inspect-adb-client
rea list-adb-devices
rea inspect-adb-device emulator-5554
rea inspect-adb-display emulator-5554
rea list-adb-features emulator-5554
rea list-adb-services emulator-5554

# Find and acquire an app (the easy-get flow)
rea resolve-adb-packages emulator-5554 whatsapp
rea list-adb-packages emulator-5554 --scope third_party
rea inspect-adb-package emulator-5554 com.whatsapp
rea pull-adb-package emulator-5554 com.whatsapp --output-directory /tmp/acq
rea inspect-android-package /tmp/acq/com.whatsapp/base.apk

# Device state and files
rea list-adb-processes emulator-5554
rea inspect-adb-window emulator-5554
rea read-adb-setting emulator-5554 global adb_enabled
rea read-adb-logcat emulator-5554 --count 200
rea list-adb-directory emulator-5554 /data/data/com.whatsapp
rea pull-adb-file emulator-5554 /data/local/tmp/notes.txt --output-directory /tmp/acq
rea push-adb-file emulator-5554 /tools/frida-server /data/local/tmp/frida-server
rea capture-adb-screen emulator-5554 --output-directory /tmp/shots
rea collect-adb-bugreport emulator-5554 --output-directory /tmp/bugs

# Package lifecycle and dynamic analysis (device-mutating)
rea install-adb-package emulator-5554 /tmp/app.apk --replace
rea start-adb-app emulator-5554 com.example.app
rea read-adb-logcat emulator-5554 --pid 12345
rea start-adb-activity emulator-5554 android.intent.action.VIEW --data-uri https://example.com
rea stop-adb-app emulator-5554 com.example.app
rea uninstall-adb-package emulator-5554 com.example.app
```

Equivalent MCP methods use the snake_case names (`list_adb_devices`,
`pull_adb_package`, `resolve_adb_packages`, …). Device operations take
`serial` exactly as `adb devices` reports it. The pulled APK set feeds the
existing analysis families directly, for example
`rea inspect-android-package /tmp/acq/<package>/base.apk`.

## Operations

| Tool                    | Kind               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `inspect_adb_client`    | read               | Resolved binary, version, install path; never contacts the server                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `list_adb_devices`      | read               | Serial, state, transport, model metadata, inferred emulator/physical kind with basis                                                                                                                                                  |
| `inspect_adb_device`    | read               | Fixed `getprop` whitelist: build, SDK, patch, fingerprint, product, ABIs, debuggable, `ro.kernel.qemu`                                                                                                                                |
| `inspect_adb_display`   | read               | `wm size` and `wm density` as declared                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `list_adb_features`     | read               | `pm list features` (hardware/software features, hex GL versions)                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `list_adb_services`     | read               | `service list` binder services and interfaces                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `list_adb_processes`    | read               | `ps -A`: user, pid, ppid, rss, state, name                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `inspect_adb_window`    | read               | `dumpsys window` focus declarations (what is on screen)                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `read_adb_setting`      | read               | One `settings get` value; device-side null is reported as such                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `read_adb_logcat`       | read               | Bounded `logcat -d -t` dump for one buffer, optional pid filter                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `list_adb_packages`     | read               | `pm list packages -f` with scope; base APK device paths                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `resolve_adb_packages`  | read               | Case-insensitive package-name substring search with exact-match flag                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `inspect_adb_package`   | read               | `dumpsys package` projection: versions, install times, installer, flags, and count of listed requested-permission rows (including Unicode names)                                                                                      |
| `list_adb_directory`    | read               | NUL-framed immediate children, including hidden entries: kinds, permissions, owner, group, sizes, symlink targets                                                                                                                     |
| `pull_adb_package`      | read               | Complete split APK set from `pm path`, each file digested                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `pull_adb_file`         | read               | One absolute device path pulled and digested                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `capture_adb_screen`    | read               | One `screencap -p` frame (exec-out, no device-side file) with dimensions                                                                                                                                                              |
| `collect_adb_bugreport` | read               | Device-generated bugreport zip, digested                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `push_adb_file`         | **mutates device** | One local file to a device path (e.g. pushing tools into `/data/local/tmp`); checks for existing targets and refuses them without explicit overwrite (the check is not atomic); compares digests when device `sha256sum` is available |
| `install_adb_package`   | **mutates device** | Local APK via `adb install [-r]`; preserves its Success/Failure verdict, records `replace_requested`, and leaves actual replacement `null` because prior package state is not observed                                                |
| `uninstall_adb_package` | **mutates device** | Requests package removal for user 0 via `adb shell pm uninstall --user 0`, without data retention                                                                                                                                     |
| `start_adb_app`         | **mutates device** | Resolves the package's launcher activity (`cmd package resolve-activity --brief`) and starts it (`am start -n`)                                                                                                                       |
| `start_adb_activity`    | **mutates device** | Starts an intent (`am start -a` with optional URI, component, and up to 16 typed extras); preserves the activity manager's verdict                                                                                                    |
| `stop_adb_app`          | **mutates device** | Force-stops every process of a package, ending a dynamic-analysis run                                                                                                                                                                 |

When `push_adb_file` receives an existing directory, adb places the local file
inside it under the local basename; Evidence reports that effective file path
while retaining the caller's directory path in the input parameters. The
private read-only staging copy preserves the source file's executable bits.

For `inspect_adb_window`, `focus_contexts` retains each display header, its exact
display ID when recognized, and every focus declaration with its original line.
Declarations without a display header are explicitly `unscoped`. A missing
declaration differs from a declaration whose `value` is JSON `null`.
`source_section` identifies the selected dumpsys section; `observed_lines`
preserves its focus declarations and display headers in source order.

`focus_summary` is `single_context` only for one context with no repeated focus
field. The singular `focused_window` and `focused_app` summarize that context;
they do not establish device-wide focus. Multiple contexts or repeated fields
produce `ambiguous` with null singular fields and all declarations retained.
When no focus field was declared, the status is `unavailable`. REA reads the
displays section only when the windows section declares neither focus field.

For `install_adb_package`, `replace_requested` records whether `-r` was sent.
The `replaced` result is `null`: the successful install response does not say
whether the package was installed fresh or replaced, and REA does not query the
device first. The install verdict and host APK digest remain available.

Push and install consume a private snapshot of the selected local input. The
reported size and SHA-256 identify those consumed bytes; `local_path` and
`apk_path` retain the original input path, whose contents may change later.
Snapshot creation needs temporary disk space proportional to the input size.
Failed snapshot cleanup remains owned and is retried before later operations
and during shutdown.

## Interpret the result

- **Package numeric declarations retain failures.** `inspect_adb_package`
  admits the first valid `userId` or `appId` as `user_id`: a nonnegative safe
  integer, including zero. A null value means no valid declaration was found.
  Malformed declarations before or after a valid value remain in
  `numeric_issues`: the first ten issues with command, field, reason and original
  `raw_line`, plus the exact `total`. Reasons are `invalid_format` or
  `unsafe_integer`. Any issue makes package coverage partial; existing section
  omissions can also make it partial. `version_code` remains exact source text.
- **Display nulls preserve uncertainty.** `inspect_adb_display` admits positive
  safe integers. Absent or malformed optional values are null; `numeric_issues`
  distinguishes malformed declarations from absence. It keeps the first ten
  issues and exact total, with command, field, original line and reason
  (`invalid_format`, `unsafe_integer` or `nonpositive`). The last recognized
  labeled declaration wins, even when malformed. A physical-density label
  suppresses bare-number fallback even when malformed; without that label, the
  first unsigned bare number wins, including zero or an unsafe integer that
  leaves the value null. Display coverage is complete only with known physical
  density and no numeric issues. Missing or malformed required physical size
  produces a protocol failure with `details.partial_observation`: an
  `inspect_adb_display` observation from provider `adb`, reason
  `physical_size_absent` or `physical_size_malformed`, and a `result` retaining
  client, serial, optional display facts, numeric issues, null physical size
  and partial coverage.
- **Directory names retain whitespace and newlines.** Symlink targets do too,
  including trailing newlines. Records containing invalid UTF-8 remain as
  labelled hex in `unparsed_lines` and make directory coverage partial.
- **Inferences carry their basis.** Device `kind` reports
  `kind_basis` (serial prefix or USB transport); APK `role` reports
  `role_basis: file_name`; `emulator_observed` is derived from the build's
  `ro.kernel.qemu` property: `true` only when its value is `"1"`, `false` for
  any other reported value, and `null` when the property is absent. The raw
  property value remains available in `properties`.
- **Device paths are not host paths.** `base_apk_device_path` values live on
  the device filesystem. Only pulls and captures produce host-local paths,
  each paired with byte size and SHA-256 digest. A pulled file's host name is
  the device path's final POSIX segment. REA preserves the original device
  path and filename; a missing final segment or `.`/`..` is refused before
  output creation. Windows hosts follow [Windows filename rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file),
  while POSIX hosts retain valid POSIX filenames such as names with spaces or
  colons. A package pull checks reported names against the destination
  filesystem before pulling, and refuses names that would share a local path.
- **Package path refusals are diagnosable.** Refusals from `pull_adb_package`
  return `unreadable_output` with `retryable: false`, keep the `pm path` output
  in `details.captured_output`, and name the refusal in `details.reason`.
  `unsafe_device_path` lists refused entries in
  `details.diagnostics.rejected_paths` as `{device_path, reason}`;
  `duplicate_local_destination` reports the shared `file_name` and both
  `device_paths`; `local_destination_unavailable` reports the `device_path`,
  `file_name`, and filesystem `error_code`. Diagnostics retain raw device
  strings, while the caller-facing message escapes invisible and bidirectional
  characters so they cannot hide text or reorder the path.
- **Splits are part of the answer.** `pm path` enumerates the base APK and
  every installed split; pulls cover the whole set. System packages whose
  APKs keep other names report the `unknown` role rather than guessing.
- **Partial results keep facts.** Failed individual pulls return successful
  artifacts with `coverage: "partial"` and per-file `failures`. Listings
  and package searches that contain unrecognized lines report the first ten
  as `unparsed_lines`, state the exact total in a limitation when more were
  seen, and mark partial coverage instead of dropping rows.
- **Mutations are explicit.** `push_adb_file`, `install_adb_package`, and
  `uninstall_adb_package` declare `mutatesTarget` and never run implicitly:
  pushes check for existing device files before transfer and refuse them
  unless `overwrite` is set. A failed or unexpected existence probe stops
  transfer even with `overwrite`; only a clean `test -e` exit of 1 with no
  output is interpreted as absence. The check is not atomic, so a different
  process can create the path before `adb push` writes it. When available, the device's
  `sha256sum` verifies the transfer. A missing command or output without a
  recognizable digest reports `device_digest_source: "unavailable"` with an
  unverified-transfer limitation; installs preserve the
  device's `Failure [...]` reason verbatim.
- **Producer identity stays attached.** Every result embeds the producing
  adb client (`binary_path`, `path_source`, `version`, `installed_path`).

## Resource and lifecycle limits

- Caller values reach adb only as positional arguments in fixed vectors;
  no tool accepts an arbitrary shell command line, `input`, or `monkey`.
  The app/activity lifecycle tools use `am start -W` and `am force-stop`.
- Per-invocation budgets: client/devices 10-20 s, shell reads 20-60 s with
  64 KiB-8 MiB capture caps (logcat 4 MiB, screen 32 MiB), transfers and
  bugreports 600 s. Output capture overflow reports `resource_constraint`
  and names the byte allowance. Deadline expiration, including the
  client-version probe, reports `provider_timeout` and names the effective
  milliseconds. This release has no runtime override for those deadlines or
  capture caps. Command cancellation preserves the caller's exact reason;
  a later abort does not replace an already completed command failure.
- Pull and capture outputs are additive: the destination must not already
  exist. Re-running a completed pull refuses the existing directory instead
  of overwriting evidence.
- Cancellation during a package pull preserves caller-selected output. The
  error includes partial observations identifying completed artifacts and the
  interrupted local path; remaining APKs were not attempted.
- Screen capture checks cancellation before publishing its exclusive output.
  If cancellation arrives after publication, the error retains the committed
  file's path, digest and dimensions; the file remains available as evidence.
- Bugreports collect into isolated staging and publish with exclusive creation;
  filename collisions select the next numeric suffix. If publication fails, the
  completed archive remains in staging. The error's partial observation gives
  its recoverable `local_path`, the original `adb_reported_path`, and an unknown
  digest status. Later operations and shutdown preserve this retained evidence.
- Failed package acquisition rollback retains its directory identity and retries
  cleanup before later work and during shutdown. Cleanup refuses a replacement
  directory. Terminal shutdown stops admission and drains active operations.
- The provider holds no long-lived processes; every invocation is one
  bounded adb run. The adb server belongs to the caller.

## Related capability and follow-up lanes

UI interaction beyond intent starts (tapping, typing, monkey fuzzing, screen
recording) remains a separate lane: candidates such as
[mobile-device-mcp](https://github.com/srmorete/mobile-device-mcp) install
driver software on the device and pair with the Frida instrumentation lane
(#1359) behind explicit mutation-authority contracts. Network transports
beyond already-connected devices (`adb connect`) are not exposed yet.

## Real verification

`npm run verify:adb` exercises every operation against a live device. It
requires `adb` (or `REA_ADB_PATH`) and any attached emulator or phone;
`--serial` selects one when several are attached, `--pull PACKAGE` pulls a
real package and verifies the returned digests against the files on disk,
and `--install-apk PATH` drives a full install → resolve → uninstall
lifecycle with a lane-owned probe.

Record: verified against adb 34.0.5 on Linux against an Android 14
(API 34) x86_64 emulator — all operations above, a 224-package inventory,
287 services, 92 features, a real two-APK split set pulled with byte-exact
digests, a verified push/pull roundtrip, a 1.3 MB screen capture, and the
complete package lifecycle; see `docs/testing.md` for the lane summary.

Intent integer extras use signed decimal text. The ADB argument encoder removes
redundant leading zeros for Android's radix-sensitive `--ei` parser while retained
Evidence keeps the caller's original spelling. Package inspection accepts both
`userId` and Android 16's `appId` spelling for the legacy `user_id` result field.

A completed push and device digest verification are separate observations. A
verification timeout, cancellation, or output budget failure returns the typed
failure with partial Evidence of the completed transfer. An unavailable checksum
command or unrecognized checksum output leaves verification explicitly unknown.

# APK signature schemes

REA reads the signing of a selected local Android APK (or ZIP/AAB) statically,
so an analyst can answer **who signed this, under which schemes, and whether the
declared content digests match these bytes** before trusting or triaging it. The reader
is in-process and needs no external engine: it parses the ZIP tail and the APK
Signing Block, reads certificates with the platform X.509 parser, and
recomputes the content digest. No Android code executes, and no device or
`adb` is involved.

CLI and MCP share one workflow and return artifact-bound Evidence inline.

```sh
rea inspect-apk-signature /path/app.apk
```

## Selected facts and retained Evidence

MCP defaults to a summary with scheme presence, signer certificate fingerprints,
row counts, posture and explicit coverage. `detail: "complete"` returns the full
report. A selected page can answer a narrower question in the acquisition call:

```json
{
  "path": "/path/app.apk",
  "view": {
    "collection": "signers",
    "schemes": ["v3"],
    "fields": ["certificate_sha256"],
    "limit": 32
  }
}
```

The returned `parent_evidence_id` identifies the retained complete report.
Subsequent reads use `inspect_analysis_view`, including after the APK is deleted:

```json
{
  "source": {
    "kind": "retained-evidence",
    "evidence_id": "<returned parent_evidence_id>"
  },
  "view": {
    "kind": "apk-signature",
    "collection": "digests",
    "signer_ids": ["<returned signer id>"],
    "fields": ["signature_algorithm_id", "algorithm", "matches_apk"],
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 32
  }
}
```

Collections are `signers`, `digests` and declared `lineage` nodes. `ids`,
`signer_ids` and `schemes` filters intersect; omitted filters select all available
records and `[]` selects none. Omitted `fields` returns every collection column;
`fields: []` retains identity and relationship links. IDs include the complete
APK digest, scheme and source ordinal; child records retain `signer_id` and
`signer_index`, and declared certificates retain their raw-DER SHA-256 identity.
Lineage pages expose `previous_id` when selected. Certificate fingerprints can
be composed across versions without treating a declaration as verified identity.

Page coverage describes examined declared records. Exhausting a page does not
establish certificate authenticity, platform acceptance, v1 entry coverage or a
verified rotation. Partial decoding and its reason remain visible even when a
lineage page contains no rows. A weak cache reuses validated immutable report
facts; each read checks its parent subject, and new file inspections read again.

CLI defaults to complete delivery. A compact one-shot response requires a complete
Evidence export:

```sh
rea inspect-apk-signature /path/app.apk --detail summary \
  --view '{"collection":"signers","fields":["certificate_sha256"]}' \
  --evidence_output /path/app-signing-evidence.json --json
```

The export contains the same complete parent used by MCP. Historical CLI pages
use `inspect-analysis-view` with an `evidence-file` source record. The CLI and MCP
share the application workflow, projection, retention and publication owners.

## What it reports

- **Schemes present:** v1 (JAR signing, from the central directory), and the
  APK Signing Block's v2, v3 and v3.1. v1 follows apksig's selection: entries
  under `META-INF/` at any depth ending in `.SF`, or in `.RSA`/`.DSA`/`.EC`
  (case-sensitive). v1 is `present` only when a signature block has its
  matching `.SF` file (`META-INF/x/CERT.RSA` pairs with `META-INF/x/CERT.SF`);
  `signature_files` and `block_files` list every candidate either way.
- **Per v1 signer** (each block paired with its `.SF`): REA inflates the block
  and reads its PKCS#7 `SignedData`. `certificate` is the certificate the
  block's one `SignerInfo` names by `issuerAndSerialNumber` or
  `subjectKeyIdentifier` (not by position), with the same facts and raw-DER
  SHA-256 as a v2/v3 signer, so a v1-only APK can be fingerprinted and
  clustered with v2/v3-signed ones. apksig resolves only
  `issuerAndSerialNumber`, so its v1 verification fails for a block whose
  `SignerInfo` uses `subjectKeyIdentifier`: REA still reports the declared
  certificate (`identified_by: subject-key-identifier`), adds a limitation,
  and treats that signer as unknown in `v1_signers_match_block_signers`. `certificates` lists every certificate the
  block carries (SHA-256 and subject) and `signer_infos` gives each
  `SignerInfo`'s certificate and digest/signature algorithm OIDs. The PKCS#7
  `SignedData` envelope is read as BER, including constructed signature OCTET
  STRINGs; each embedded certificate is still interpreted as DER by the X.509
  owner. Issuer matching preserves the encoded Name and also admits equivalent
  ASCII PrintableString/UTF8String values for CN, C, L, ST, O and OU: case and
  repeated/edge spaces are normalized, RDN sequence order is preserved, and
  attribute order inside one multivalued RDN is ignored. Other name forms
  require exact encoded identity; semantic equivalence remains unestablished.
  `certificate` is `null` when the block has more than one `SignerInfo` (with
  nothing verified there is no single signer) or names a certificate it does
  not carry. A block that cannot be read (malformed ASN.1, an unsupported
  compression method, Zip64 sizes, a local header that disagrees with the
  central directory on the name, data-descriptor flag, CRC-32 or a size, as
  apksig refuses it, or over a bound) keeps its names and carries
  `decode_error`; it is never reported as an absent signer. apksig ignores
  the ZIP encryption flag (bit 0), so a block that sets it is read as stored:
  the PKCS#7 decoding decides (bytes that really are encrypted fail to
  decode), and a limitation names the block.
  apksig rejects the v1 signature of an archive whose central directory
  holds any name more than once ("Duplicate entry"). REA checks every entry:
  a limitation names the first few duplicates (JSON-quoted; a name over 256
  bytes is cut there and its stored length given) and counts the rest, and a
  signer whose block, `.SF` or `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` name is duplicated
  (one signer per block name) carries `decode_error`
  `duplicate entry: <name>`, so a duplicated manifest marks every signer.
  A duplicate outside those names leaves the signers as declared.
  Names are compared as apksig compares them, as Java strings decoded from
  UTF-8: malformed bytes become U+FFFD, so `dup\xff` and `dup\xfe` are one
  name (apksigner: `Duplicate entry: dup�`). REA reproduces Java's
  replacement rather than WHATWG `TextDecoder`'s; the two differ for encoded
  surrogates (`ED A0..BF`), which Java replaces as one unit. This was checked
  against OpenJDK 25's `new String(bytes, UTF_8)` on about 300,000 malformed
  and well-formed sequences, including a leading byte-order mark, which Java
  keeps; other Java runtimes are not checked. The same
  decoding names v1 entries and compares a local header's name with the
  central directory's; as in apksig, a local name longer in bytes than the
  directory's is refused before decoding. apksig takes the record count from the classic
  end-of-central-directory record's 16-bit field and ignores a Zip64 count,
  so it reads only the first 65,535 records of a larger directory: the
  limitation then says so, counts as duplicates for apksig only names whose
  second copy lies within those records, and names separately those
  duplicated only past them. REA still reads v1 signing entries, and flags
  duplicated signing names, from every record, so past record 65,535 it
  reports signers apksig would not see.
  Bytes after the block's `ContentInfo` are ignored, as apksig's BER parser
  ignores them, and a limitation names the block and their count.
- **Per signer:** the certificate's **SHA-256 fingerprint over the raw embedded
  DER** (the same value `apksigner --print-certs` prints), plus subject, issuer,
  serial, ISO 8601 validity and public-key algorithm when the X.509 parser can
  read the exact carried DER (each is `null` otherwise). The parser's returned
  DER must equal those bytes before readable facts are combined with their
  fingerprint; embedded PEM text and trailing data cannot select a different
  certificate. Raw signature algorithm IDs, declared
  digest hex and digest algorithms, signature lengths and public-key length; and for
  v3/v3.1 the signer's declared min/max SDK.
- **Key rotation (v3/v3.1):** the declared proof-of-rotation lineage, oldest
  first. Each node carries its certificate and the capability flags **retained
  by that node's own certificate** after rotation (installed data, shared UID,
  permission, rollback, auth). A lineage attribute that cannot be decoded is
  reported with `decode_error`, never silently emptied.
- **Source stamp:** whether a source-stamp block is present and the stamp
  certificate it declares (the V2 stamp block is preferred over V1, as apksig
  does). `certificate` is `null` when no stamp is present, or when the block
  could not be decoded and `decode_error` says why. Stamp signatures are not
  verified.
- **Declared digest consistency:** for SHA-256/SHA-512 digests, REA recomputes
  the v2/v3 content digest and reports `matches_apk` per digest and
  `posture.self_consistent`. This only shows that the **declared** digest
  equals the digest of the current bytes. It is **not a signature
  verification**: anyone who changes the bytes can recompute the digest and
  write it into the signed data, and REA still reports `true` while
  `apksigner verify` rejects the APK. A changed byte with an unchanged
  declared digest reads `false`.
- **Posture** (derived from the facts above):
  - `v1_only`: v1 is present and no v2/v3/v3.1 block is. The v1
    `X-Android-APK-Signed` marker is not read, so this cannot distinguish an
    APK signed only with v1 from one whose v2/v3 block was removed.
  - `schemes_agree_on_signer` (observed): every present block scheme presents
    the same _set_ of signer certificates. An extra signer in one scheme is
    disagreement; a signer without a certificate makes it `null` (unknown).
    Build-tools 33+ rotate through v3.1 by default, so a rotated app usually
    reads `false` here and `true` below.
  - `signer_change_declared_by_rotation` (declared): the signers differ, but
    each appears in a lineage the APK declares. Read the two together: a
    rotated APK shows `false` / `true`; signers that differ with no declared
    lineage containing them show `false` / `false`. It is `null` when a
    signer's identity is unknown, or when the signers differ and a declared
    lineage could not be decoded.
  - `v1_signers_match_block_signers` (observed): the v1 signer certificates
    equal what the lowest block scheme that has signers (v2, else v3, else
    v3.1) expects v1 to carry. That is its signer set, except that a v3/v3.1
    signer declaring a rotation lineage expects the lineage's first
    (original) certificate, as apksig requires. `false` is notable: the JAR
    signature names a different key than the block signature. A key rotation
    keeps v1 (and v2) on the original key, so it reads `true` while
    `schemes_agree_on_signer` reads `false`, with or without v2. `null` when
    v1 or a block scheme is absent, any signer's identity is unknown (a
    `decode_error`, a `null` certificate or a `subjectKeyIdentifier`
    `SignerInfo`), or the lineage's original certificate cannot be
    identified; a limitation then says why.
  - `strongest_scheme`, `rotation_present`, `source_stamp_present`,
    `self_consistent`.

## What it does not claim

This is **declared identity and digest consistency, not trust**. No signature
is cryptographically verified (including the v1 PKCS#7 signature and the
`.SF`/`MANIFEST.MF` digests, so a v1 signer is reported even where `keytool`
or `apksigner` reject the archive), certificate chains and revocation are not
evaluated, and nothing here says an app is authentic. `self_consistent: true`
means the declared digest equals the digest of the current bytes; it is not a
signature verification, and it does not prove who made the bytes. Rotation-lineage node signatures are not verified either, so a lineage is
what the APK _declares_: an attacker who re-signs an APK can declare any
lineage, which is why `signer_change_declared_by_rotation` is kept apart from
the observed agreement. SHA-256 identifies exact bytes, not authenticity.

Not yet read: v4 `.apk.idsig` (a sibling file), verity (`0x0421`/`0x0423`/`0x0425`) digests (reported with
`matches_apk: null`), and the v1 `X-Android-APK-Signed` marker.

## Bounds and errors

The archive is read once, bounded at 512 MiB, without following symlinks and
with change detection. ZIP tail offsets, the central-directory size and signing
block spans used by the reader are checked against their containing sections,
including the complete central-directory extent before ZIP end records. A process-wide queue permits
one active whole-file inspection and eight pending scans across provider
instances; pending scans retain no APK bytes and can be cancelled with their
original reason. Further requests receive a capacity error. The active slot
is held through parsing and cleanup. Signers per scheme, v1 signers and
lineage nodes are capped at 32 each as resource admission limits, not format
maxima (apksig separately accepts at most 10 v1 signers). Each v1 block is
inflated to at most 1 MiB, and its BER is read within 32 levels of nesting and
65,536 elements, with at most 32 certificates and 32 `SignerInfo`s; BER
indefinite lengths and constructed OCTET STRING fields are accepted. Embedded
X.509 certificates retain their DER requirement. The report's size is
bounded from above by those counts before anything is materialised, and the exact
serialized size of the report together with its limitations (which repeat
archive names) is then checked against an 8 MiB output budget (the exact check
is authoritative); an over-budget report is refused, not truncated.

The whole-file reader allocates the selected snapshot and bounded read scratch;
total process memory exceeds the selected file's size. It also computes the complete
file SHA-256, so inspection is not header-only. Content digests are recomputed
at most once per SHA-256/SHA-512 algorithm during one inspection. Input,
inflation, decoded-record and serialized-output bounds keep work finite;
resource refusals are distinct from malformed format errors.

If the stable read completes but closing its descriptor fails or is cancelled,
the error retains `details.partial_observation` with the selected path, complete
file SHA-256 and byte count. These facts describe the acquired file; they do not
establish any decoded signing facts. Failed cleanup remains visible until the
provider releases the descriptor on a cleanup retry.

A file that is not a ZIP is refused as an unsupported target. A damaged ZIP
(local headers but no end-of-central-directory), a central directory that
cannot be walked or whose declared record count does not account for all of
its bytes, or a malformed signing block or signer is an input error naming the
offset or scheme and reason. Zip64 tail damage includes a missing required
locator, an impossible locator disk/count pair, a fixed end record that does
not fit before its locator, or an incorrect end-record signature. These are
input errors, not evidence of an unsupported format. Coherent multi-disk
locator metadata and 64-bit offsets/counts/sizes beyond the reader's safe
integer range remain unsupported. The locator offset is disk-relative, so
multi-disk metadata is checked before applying local file bounds. This follows
the record fields in [PKWARE APPNOTE 6.3.10, sections 4.3.14–4.3.15](https://pkware.cachefly.net/webdocs/casestudies/APPNOTE.TXT);
it does not establish full validation of Zip64 versions or extensible data.
Signer framing includes signature records, the public-key field and matching
signed/outer v3 SDK ranges. Suffix bytes beyond known
fields are counted as uninterpreted, as Android readers may ignore extensions;
their presence does not establish malformed signing.
When the central directory is not immediately followed by
the end-of-central-directory record (a declared-size mismatch or a Zip64
record), the content digest is not recomputed and a limitation says so. A
rotation attribute that cannot be decoded still counts as `rotation_present`
(the attribute exists) and carries its `decode_error`.

Verified by the `verify:apk-signature` real lane. It builds a real minimal APK
with `aapt2`, signs it with the SDK's `apksigner` (default v2+v3, v1-only with
RSA and EC keys, v1+v2+v3 on a legacy target, a rotated key lineage with and
without v1, rotation carried by v3.1, a source stamp, and a copy
with one changed byte), and cross-checks REA against
`apksigner verify --print-certs`, `apksigner lineage --print-certs` and
`keytool -printcert -jarfile` through the CLI and MCP.

The real-toolchain CI lane uses pinned, checksum-verified Build Tools 36.1.0
and platform 36 oracle files in its job workspace. It requires the existing
host JDK and runs `npm run verify:apk-signature -- --require-tools`; absent
oracles fail rather than silently establishing provider coverage. REA itself
requires none of these external tools.

# Apktool resource decoding

REA decodes Android resource tables and the binary manifest through the
caller's Apktool launcher. This completes the static triad for Android
targets: Java/Kotlin sources through the JADX family, engine-grade
decompilation through JEB, and resources through this family. REA never
installs Apktool or a Java runtime.

## Supply tools

Use Apktool 2.7.0 or newer (verified with 2.7.0 and 3.0.3 on Linux) and a Java runtime the
launcher can find. Select the launcher through the environment:

```sh
# Optional: absolute path to the apktool launcher (upstream wrapper or a
# java -jar script); without it, apktool resolves from PATH.
export REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND=/absolute/path/apktool
```

Readiness is `rea inspect-apktool-client`: it runs `apktool --version` and
reports the resolved launcher, its selection source, and its version. A
missing launcher reports `capability_unavailable` with the
`REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND` remediation rather than attempting an installation.
`binary_session` uses the same host probe for tool availability; it does not
validate a particular APK or guarantee that the selected input can be decoded.

Client inspection and decode results disclose the following reported-version
advisory windows without refusing otherwise compatible launchers:

| Advisory                                                                                              | Reported version window                          | Host scope |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------- |
| [CVE-2024-21633](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/security/advisories/GHSA-2hqv-2xv4-5h5w)      | Before 2.9.2                                     | All        |
| [GHSA-vgwr-4w3p-xmjv](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/security/advisories/GHSA-vgwr-4w3p-xmjv) | Before 2.9.3                                     | Windows    |
| [CVE-2026-39973](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/security/advisories/GHSA-m8mh-x359-vm8m)      | 3.0.0 release line through versions before 3.0.2 | All        |

The 2026 advisory names 3.0.1 and its 3.0.2 fix. Inclusion of 3.0.0 is
source-derived: [tagged 3.0.0](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/blob/f770b39e425af4fa6ac4ca1e9ea6c4824339c6d3/brut.apktool/apktool-lib/src/main/java/brut/androlib/res/table/ResTypeSpec.java)
passes type names through unchanged; the [3.0.2 patch](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/commit/65dd8480dfcb63068562ffaa527f71bb0a9f772c)
validates those names at their owner before they reach the output-path producer.
Prereleases before the fixed release are conservatively disclosed; the exact
`-dirty` downstream marker is compared as a release while preserving its spelling.
This is version guidance, not verification of a particular prerelease or decoder.

A launcher version does not prove the decoder's contents, execution platform,
downstream backports, or overall safety. Windows applicability uses the selected
local host; an opaque wrapper may run another engine. A missing warning means
only that none of these version/host windows matched. Verify the selected
decoder's patches before decoding untrusted APKs; the compatibility floor above
is not a security recommendation. REA does not fetch advisories at runtime.

On Windows, a `.bat` or `.cmd` launcher (such as Chocolatey's `apktool.bat`)
runs through an explicit `cmd.exe /d /s /c` call. That call has no AutoRun,
no delayed expansion, and quotes every argument. A launcher path that
contains `"`, `%`, `^`, `!`, `&`, `|`, `<` or `>` is reported as
`not_configured` instead of being passed to `cmd.exe`. If REA's temporary
decode paths contain those characters, decoding through a batch launcher
reports `capability_unavailable`.

## Answer an analyst question

```sh
rea inspect-apktool-client
rea decode-android-resources /targets/Example.apk
rea decode-android-resources /targets/Example.apk --locale de
rea decode-android-resources /targets/Example.apk --locales de --locales pt-BR
rea decode-android-resources /targets/Example.apk --locales de --locales pt-BR --string-tables-only
rea decode-android-resources /targets/Example.apk --no-strings
rea decode-android-resources /targets/Example.apk --decode-timeout-ms 900000
```

Equivalent MCP methods are `inspect_apktool_client` and
`decode_android_resources`. The decode request takes `path`, an optional
primary `locale` (project `res/values-<locale>/strings.xml` instead of the default
table), `locales` (repeatable array of additional localized string tables to project
from the same single decode pass), and `include_strings` (default true). Regional locales such as `pt-BR`
select Android's `values-pt-rBR`. A three-digit region such as `es-419`
selects `values-b+es+419`; `es-r419` is rejected because Android's legacy
`-r` form requires a two-letter region. Android qualifiers such as `pt-rBR`
and `b+zh+Hans+CN` may also be supplied directly.

Set `string_tables_only: true` (CLI `--string-tables-only`) to return string
entries only inside `string_tables`, including when selecting a single table.
The top-level `strings` array is then empty by request; it does not establish
that the primary table is empty. Table status, counts and coverage still describe
the examined source. This avoids repeating primary entries in multi-locale
responses and charges the aggregate output budget for one copy per table.
Omitting the option preserves existing responses. `include_strings: false`
still suppresses all string projection, including in this mode.

## Interpret the result

- **An owned APK snapshot is digested and decoded.** `target.sha256` and
  `target.bytes` bind the observation to the exact APK that was decoded.
  The Evidence subject carries the same snapshot digest and caller-selected
  path, including when the original file changes during decoding.
  A change during snapshot acquisition reports retryable `artifact_changed`;
  wait for a stable input before retrying. Host read permission failures report
  `access_denied`, while a missing or non-regular selected path reports
  `invalid_request` with the rejected `path` field.
- **Metadata comes from apktool.yml as apktool printed it.** Version codes
  keep their own spelling (`'7'` versus `7`); `package_name` is read from
  the decoded manifest, not inferred.
  Apktool 3's emitted `version: 3.x.y` header selects its single-line string
  dialect: literal hashes, single quotes, empty strings, and the text `null`
  stay part of the value; producer backslashes and Unicode escapes decode
  once. Older/tagged documents retain YAML scalar semantics; double-quoted
  values also retain YAML string semantics.
  This distinction follows the released
  [3.0.3 metadata writer](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/blob/18b5e99cb56ff9451e8aa55b065dcf5bbd616975/brut.apktool/apktool-lib/src/main/java/brut/androlib/meta/VersionInfo.java#L49-L55)
  and [string escape owner](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/blob/18b5e99cb56ff9451e8aa55b065dcf5bbd616975/brut.j.yaml/src/main/java/brut/yaml/YamlStringEscapeUtils.java#L55-L116).
- **The manifest is the decoded text**, bounded at 512 KiB and reported as
  truncated when larger.
- **Strings are projected verbatim.** Escaped entities stay escaped, and
  entries containing nested markup (`<b>`, `<xliff:g>`) are counted as
  unparsed rather than flattened — the limitation names the examined count.
  Malformed XML and a wrong document root are whole-document projection
  failures: the result is partial, the failure reason is disclosed, and entry
  counts remain unknown. They are not counted as one unsupported string.
  The default table is bounded to 2000 entries with partial coverage when more
  exist. `locales` lists observed regular `strings.xml` tables whose exact
  `values-<locale>` directory is selectable by the request's locale grammar.
  Locale suffixes allow up to 23 ASCII characters, derived from Apktool's
  language, script, region, and variant fields; for example,
  `b+sr+Latn+RS+REVISED` selects that exact table.
  Other table directories, including combined qualifiers such as
  `values-en-rUS-v21` and `values-mcc310-fr`, are named in limitations with
  their source spelling. They are not advertised as selectable locales;
  REA does not infer Android's runtime resource matching. Non-regular
  strings-table paths are disclosed with partial coverage. Discovery uses
  the same bounded traversal as the file count; filesystem failures remain
  failures rather than being interpreted as missing tables.
  When multiple tables are requested with `locales`, `string_tables` records
  each projected table with its locale, status (`present`, `missing`,
  `oversized`, `malformed`, or `skipped`), entry counts, and coverage,
  bounded at an aggregate budget of 10,000 strings and 32 MiB XML. When `locales`
  is omitted and `string_tables_only` is not true, legacy single-table payloads are preserved
  without adding `string_tables`.
- **Smali is skipped by design** (`apktool d --no-src`): Java-source
  recovery belongs to the JADX family. Resource smali edits and rebuild are
  a follow-up lane with mutation authority.
- **Workspaces are owned and short-lived.** Decoding happens in a
  provider-owned temporary directory that is removed before the result is
  returned. The APK snapshot and framework cache both live inside this directory.
  If removal fails, the result names the residual path and the provider retains
  ownership for a cleanup retry on close, including failed decodes.

## Resource and lifecycle limits

- The decode wall clock is `decode_timeout_ms` (CLI `--decode-timeout-ms`).
  Omitted means 600000 ms. The integer range is 1 to 2147483647. A change
  applies on the next decode. It does not raise the 4194304-byte (4 MiB)
  output capture budget. That capture budget has no runtime override. A
  stopped decode reports `provider_timeout` and names the effective
  milliseconds; an exceeded capture budget reports `resource_constraint`.
- The version probe waits 20000 ms and retains 65536 bytes. This release has
  no runtime override for that probe. `decode_timeout_ms` does not raise it.
- Manifest reads are bounded to 512 KiB before decoding UTF-8. Strings XML
  reads are bounded to 8 MiB; larger documents are skipped with partial
  coverage and an explicit limit, rather than reported as missing.
- `decoded_file_count` is capped at 100,000 files; the cap is reported in
  the limitations when hit.
- An ordinary nonzero decode exit surfaces as `unsupported_target` naming
  the caller-selected APK, with Apktool's diagnostic and captured output.
  Launcher startup, ownership preparation, signal termination and incomplete
  output collection remain provider failures; they do not establish that the
  selected APK is unsupported.

## Real verification

`npm run verify:apktool -- --apk PATH` exercises both operations against a
real launcher. Record: apktool 2.7.0-dirty (Debian packaging) on Linux with
OpenJDK 25 against a signed aapt2-built probe APK carrying two resource
locales — launcher version, on-disk digest agreement, apktool.yml metadata
(1.2.3, SDK 24–34), manifest package agreement, default and `de` string
tables projected. Parser goldens in the test suite come from the same
decode. See `docs/testing.md` for the lane summary.

Multi-locale and table-only projection were also verified through real CLI and
stdio MCP workflows on Linux with Apktool 3.0.3/JDK 21 against NewPipe 0.29.1,
ApiDemos 6.0.18 and Appium Settings 8.2.1. Independent XML projection checks,
exact facts/Evidence parity and bounded task costs are recorded in the
[shared-decode and table-only checkpoint](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/42e1a17d6e6c0487f17be0bae248553c4caba7f7/experiments/analysis-efficiency/apktool-string-tables.md).
This qualifies selected resource facts, not application execution or independent
binary resource-decoder completeness.

If the selected APK changes while its private snapshot is copied, acquisition
returns `artifact_changed`; request-schema correction cannot recover a stable
snapshot. Launcher spawn permission denial is distinct from a missing launcher,
and configuration diagnostics retain the selected command and system error.
